_"Hello Mr. Bocobza_

_Thank you for reaching out to us. We initiated an internal process to confirm your opt-out requests and confirmed that your direct marketing preferences remained unchanged until the 26th of February, when they were changed manually by our team. To ensure, we repeated the process and removed you from all direct marketing communications again as of 29th of February._

_Please be aware that Bolt is not available in Israel and does not support Hebrew. Similarly, Bolt does not operate in the USA and, therefore, is not subject to the jurisdictions of the CCPA as amended by the CPRA. Bolt's services are primarily offered within the EU and selected other jurisdictions. Consequently, we commit to adhering only to the legal requirements applicable in our areas of operation, including the GDPR, the Directive 2002/58/EC, their local implementing laws, and any other relevant local legislation._

_Please note that our procedures on direct marketing are very strict and are designed to comply with the applicable laws. Specifically:_

_1] We only send direct marketing to existing customers in accordance with Article 13(2) of the Directive 2002/58/EC, providing the opportunity for opt-out consent._

_2] It is only not possible to unsubscribe from service-related communications, as these communications are critical for maintaining the security, functionality, and legal compliance of the service, in accordance with the applicable laws._

_3] We inform customers of the possibility to opt out of direct marketing both at the moment of registration (via communication settings - which are available to you at any time in the Bolt Rides application) - and in each communication channel via means affecting the particular channel._

_4] To be more specific, each direct marketing email must contain an unsubscribe link in the footer; each SMS includes instructions that you can unsubscribe by responding "STOP", etc._

_5] In all cases falling outside of the exemption in Article 13(2), such as promoting the offers of our partners, we will always request your opt-in consent._

_6] We clearly indicate the identity of the data controller in the footer, as required by applicable laws._

_7] Please note that the requirement from Israeli law to include the word "advertising" (פרסומת) in the emails' headline should not be applicable, as per our explanation above._

_We will keep monitoring your account for any signs of previous technical issues. Currently, you should not receive any direct marketing communications, as we have manually opted you out. We hope our message clarifies the situation and addresses your concerns.”_

        AND a.support_case_created_date_utc < DATE('2024-02-01')
        AND a.has_ai_solution_attempt 
),
predicted_issues AS (
    SELECT 
        b.support_case_id,
        JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR(JSON_ARRAY_GET(JSON_EXTRACT(e.event_data, '$.issues'), 0), '$.issue') AS top_predicted_issue,
        JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR(JSON_ARRAY_GET(JSON_EXTRACT(e.event_data, '$.issues'), 0), '$.probability') AS top_predicted_issue_probability
    FROM base AS b
    LEFT JOIN ng_customer_support.support_case_event AS e
        ON e.created_date >= DATE('2024-01-01')
            AND e.event_type = 'user_issue_prediction_result'
            AND e.support_case_id = b.support_case_id
),
actual_issues AS (
    SELECT 
        b.support_case_id,
        ARRAY_AGG(i.issue_key) AS actual_issue_keys
    FROM base AS b
    LEFT JOIN ng_customer_support.fact_support_case_issue_keys AS i
        ON i.issue_created_date >= DATE('2024-01-01')
            AND i.support_case_id = b.support_case_id
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT 
    b.*,
    p.top_predicted_issue,
    p.top_predicted_issue_probability,
    a.actual_issue_keys,
    c.is_support_case_escalated_to_agent
FROM base AS b
LEFT JOIN predicted_issues AS p
    ON p.support_case_id = b.support_case_id
LEFT JOIN actual_issues AS a
    ON a.support_case_id = b.support_case_id
LEFT JOIN core_models.fact_support_case AS c
    ON c.support_case_id = b.support_case_id
        AND c.support_case_created_date_utc = b.support_case_created_date_utc{noformat}

[~accountid:712020:ab95f96b-73f1-4bb8-a5fd-5178ef3f1339] here are my thoughts:

* TVDE law establishes a  broad prohibition of publicity in TVDE vehicles. 
* The Bolt green colour is included in trademark registrations of Bolt in conjunction with the word. The symbol of Bolt is also a registered trademark.
* Additionally this law specifically points out that TVDE vehicles shall “_circulate without any external sign indicating the type of service they provide, with the exception of a badge, visible from the outside and removable, in terms to be defined by decision of the IMT_”. This obligation should be read in the context of what is understood as ride-hailing by this same law, which is “the activity of individual and remunerated passenger transport in *uncharacterised* vehicles from an electronic platform”.
* This leads me to conclude that vehicles with original green colour from the car manufactured can be used in TVDE in PT, and it would not be considered branding. On the contrary,  using the Bolt green colour to paint the vehicles would more likely than not be under the general prohibition of publicity. It also could arguably be considered that those vehicles would not be uncharacterised.

I hope this clarifies.

Hey [~accountid:63fe21787c30bbd6b33e09d3],

Signup offers are available to all new users, meaning the only pre-requisite is to not have been using Bolt before.

We’re interested only in advertising disclaimer requirements for this new-user offer. As you can see Uber only discloses the monetary value of the promotion and the amount of times you can use it (one, I assume). the rest of the terms are hidden behind a simple “terms apply”, which I again assume, would be available to see in full in-app.

Can also limit the disclaimer to just “terms apply” or is that illegal and we have to disclose more information straight away (such as end date, max discount per trip, valid locations, etc.) 



Long T&C disclaimer would be fine for most advertising platforms as there’s room to put them. The only problematic one would be Google Ads, as the way ads are generated on the platform is – we upload several headlines, several descriptions, and several images, and then Google mix-and-matches them to create dozens of variations. Just putting the full T&C on the images might not suffice as some ad placements would have only the headline and/or description. And description character limits do not allow us to put the full T&Cs there. And for headlines, even “Terms apply” wouldn’t fit.

So again, we’re looking to find out what would be the legal bare minimum of terms disclosure within the ad for the signup offers (granted that the full terms are available in-app) 

could we do just “-X% for your first X rides” 

or “-X% for your first X rides. Terms apply” like we see Uber do

or then “-X% for your first X rides. (followed by a whole paragraph of terms)” 



Let me know if you need any additional info on how the ads are shown to the users.

Many thanks!

Hi [~accountid:610a3ee66051c5006aeeeea1] 

Me and [~accountid:712020:0641ea87-e832-482b-8673-ab85e9ad6441] have finished our revision of this ticket and would like to share our conclusions with you, before sending it to César. 

Regarding César’s questions we have concluded the following: 

* Taxi services are regulated by a Law that was amended last October. The new Law has specific provisions that regard the provision of these services through electronic platforms. Therefore, as there is sector-specific legislation the provisions on the law that regulates general contractual clauses is only subsidiarily applicable. Moreover, we have concluded that the Consumer’s Right Directive and its national transposition are not applicable in this case, as they are only applicable to contracts with final consumers. 
* Among several things, the Taxi Law establishes the fees applicable to Taxi services. These fees are the ones reflected on the "_Documento de Cálculo de Preço de Viagem_", the document that César is asking us about. Thus, this document does not contain any sensible or confidential information but rather only the fees established by Law  (we have confirmed with César and he agrees that there is no confidential information). Therefore, we see no problem in this document being publicly shared. 
* The easiest way to share it, and that would result in less work for César’s team, would be to make this document available together with the Taxi T&Cs. This would ensure that, on one hand, users have access to the document before accepting the T&Cs (which is a legal requirement, per Taxi Law and DL 446/85 - party must have full knowledge of the terms before accepting it) and, on the other hand, the process of sharing the document would be more automatic. 
* We also would advice them to create a feature for the T&Cs (with this Fee Annex) to be automatically sent by email after the account is activated, in order to ensure that the document is kept in a semi-durable format - which is a legal requirement per Taxi Law and DL 7/2004. 
* Regarding Bolt’s fees (which are not reflected in the legal fees shared through the document in question), we have concluded that these are already shared by email, which is fine according to the law. 

(More information on the comments below)

In conclusion, the answer to César questions would be: 

# *_Would it be possible to include the "Documento de Cálculo de Preço de Viagem" as an Attachment to the Taxi Operators T&Cs_**?* Yes, there is no legal provision prohibiting that. 
# *I**_f we include this document either in the T&C's or the Life Cycle Comms after a fleet is signed up, could we consider that this document is delivered with this method?_* Yes, if the Document is next to the T&Cs, when the user accepts the T&Cs they are automatically accepting the Annex. Anyway, after fleet registration an automatic email should be sent containing the T&Cs + Annex, in order to fulfil the legal requirement of a semi-durable mean of conservation of the Contract. 

Do you agree? 

Thank you

Hi Mihai*,*

We are writing in relation to your request dated *19/2/2024.*

We do not have access to, or store your card details when you use Apple Pay. Your device gives a token reference to the card (not the actual card number) to merchants, such as Bolt in this instance, which is issued by the bank during authentication and then used for any payment through Apple Pay.

When you accept an order and it is authorised with Apple Pay, Bolt uses this token to manage payments in the context of the requested service.

In summary, your card number and identity are not shared with Bolt. When you pay, neither Apple nor your device will send your actual card number to merchants such as Bolt.

Please note that payments related to the order are charged according to our Terms and Conditions (for in-app payments Clauses 3.1 to 3.6). The Bolt app may begin charging a fare on a waiting time basis (Clause 4.6).

We ensure that all of our payments are in line with PSD2, acquirer rules and other applicable regulations.

Apple, Inc. (United States) is not our provider for taking payments. We do not have any contractual relationship with this provider.

In reference to your request for a copy of your personal data, the password-protected files were shared on 25/1/2024, now re-attached with this correspondence.

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

Yours sincerely,
Bolt

Bolt Market needs our expertise to manage picker’s queues since in a lot of ways it can be considered as similar to managing courier queues. Currently pickers take orders to pick in a FIFO fashion. This can be suboptimal - for example, let’s say that we already decided to batch 2 orders but one of the orders in the batch is first one in the picking queue and the other one is last in the picking queue. The first order will wait a significant time for the other order to be picked, but if we optimised the picker queues a bit, we could reduce the overall delivery times for certain orders.

# We want to prepare for the migration to TiDB where the collation is binary, not case insensitive

Current logic can be summarized like this:
Users who make more than 240 requests to {{getRideOptions}} per hour sustained, over a period of 12 hours, are marked as bot. If the user makes more than 400 requests to getRideOptions they get blocked at 6 hours.

{code:sql}SELECT
    freq.user_id,
    SUM(freq.hits_per_hour) AS matches,
    COUNT(*)                AS hours_per_day,
    MIN(freq.hits_per_hour) AS min_reqs_per_hour
FROM (
         SELECT
             search_categories_overview__user_id                    AS user_id,
             EXTRACT(HOUR FROM search_categories_overview__created) AS hour,
                    COUNT(*)                                               AS hits_per_hour
         FROM glue.ng_public.etl_search_denormalized_view
         WHERE
             created_date >= DATE_ADD('DAY', -1, CURRENT_DATE)
         GROUP BY 1, 2
         HAVING COUNT(*) > 240
         ORDER BY hits_per_hour DESC
             LIMIT 2400
     ) AS freq
GROUP BY user_id
HAVING
    (COUNT(*) > 12)
    OR (COUNT(*) > 6 AND MIN(freq.hits_per_hour) > 480)
ORDER BY matches DESC
    LIMIT 100;{code}

Creating a Presto service user for you is possible, but we only want to leave that as a last resort. We do it only in exceptional cases when nothing else can be done. 

There are a couple of caveats related to the programmatic Presto user:

# We don’t provide any SLAs for that type of access - Presto can go down, become slow or unresponsive at any moment.

A different option we’d like you to consider is using Scheduled Reporting [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/3679682625/Export+data+from+the+data+lake+with+Scheduled+Reporting|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/3679682625/Export+data+from+the+data+lake+with+Scheduled+Reporting|smart-link]. This is a tool to periodically extract data from the Data Lake to an arbitrary S3 bucket that can be later easily and quickly queried from the backend. This seems to be a better option IMO, from the backed perspective, because reading an S3 bucket is much more solid and quicker than querying Presto.

Hi [~accountid:712020:d3fd53e6-f124-4770-a577-b09d6688566f] - in short, yes, this would create reclassification issues.

The vehicle type ought to be at the choice of the passenger, based on pricing etc. We can’t prioritise one vehicle over another for our own agenda without impacting the ability of non-EV drivers to get work. Unfortunately, would have the effect of ‘managing a workforce’ for Bolt’s own benefit. This runs contrary to our defence narrative that Bolt works *_for_* drivers (which is technically correct and as it should be). 

For reference, we have already been asked in litigation whether we prioritise any types of driver - so it does come up. 

Generally, any prioritisation that isn’t based on ETA, or where we are otherwise treating drivers differently based on any performance standards (or really on anything for our own benefit) is going to be scrutinised in markets where reclassification claims are made. 

It would therefore be ideal to promote EVs in other ways, especially in riskier markets.

Alternatively, if this is activity is business critical, there is generally less reclassification risk in {color:#4c9aff}‘{color}[{color:#4c9aff}Implementation Class 1’ markets{color}|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1iRAIxZgCb9EAGtb6nPaPsRG4ExKL-OGSaYcFhz49SNc/edit#gid=0] - which are perceived to have a lower likelihood of claims. There will still be risk associated with this and we ought to avoid stacking any markets with risk unless it’s truly necessary.

At first instance, I’d consider your alternatives for promoting EVs. If you did want to proceed with this, then we can raise the topic for discussion in our ‘reclassification committee’ - but it ought to be accompanied by short ‘business case’ so that we can properly assess the pros and cons.

I will close this ticket for now but please reach out if you would like additional advice on the subject. Many thanks.

Payments flow:
- Booking fee is setup. [https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/pricing-config/city/79/booking-fees/53|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/pricing-config/city/79/booking-fees/53]. This means that each ride from Schiphol receives the schiphol Booking fee. No commission is taken on the booking fee and it is incl VAT.
- This booking fee is paid by the customer.
- This amount is included for the driver in his total revenue. However it is than deducted in equal amount labelled as the Schiphol booking fee. 
- On a monthly basis an invoice is generated by Axxicom based on the trips completed x the booking fee.
- We pay the invoice. 

In summary, the fee is paid by rider to the driver on his balance. It is than deducted as Airport booking fee. On monthly basis Axxicom sends the invoice, which we done pay based on the airport rides x booking fee.

Best, Lars

* *Hiding PII data* behind anonymised view.

This is a blocker for the fraud team right now. We have PII-containing tables with big data volumes (from few thousand per month to 150m rows/month), which we need to keep as PII for analytical purposes (to create/adjust anti-fraud rules). Because the data is PII, we can’t use it in Looker dashboards directly. But we would like to measure (in Looker) weekly, how much the rules are triggering and how many false positives (friction for good users who were falsely marked as fraudsters by our rules) we are causing. So this can have big negative impact on GMV and UX if our false positive rates get out of hand.

Currently we have solved this issue by creating Presto views, but since the Presto views are maintained manually by the ingestion team, modifying/adding new views creates additional workload for them. Could become a bottleneck if more teams start using this workaround.

Hi [~accountid:5d53a63ba1f3290c16e637d6] 

There is no legal ‘obligation’ to follow through on a promise, however some promises can be deemed to be legally binding under certain conditions. Generally, for a promise to be legally enforceable, it must meet the requirements of a valid contract. 

In the circumstance that you explain above, I would suggest approaching these kinds of matters pragmatically. If a CS agent “promises” to make a payment to a Driver and/or Passenger and then another CS agent does not follow through on that “promise” it does not appear to be good from a User experience that the information that Bolt is providing them is inconsistent. 

Ultimately, it is a business decision on how these matters should be handled as opposed to legal teams decision. However, if a promise has been made in error and you want to go back on the promise (i.e. not fulfil the promise, such as making a payment etc) you should bear in mind that if the Driver or the Passenger decided to pursue a claim against Bolt in court, these inconsistent communications could be used as evidence against Bolt, therefore weakening any defence that Bolt could raise. 

I would suggest maybe putting in preventative measures to avoid these inconsistent communications pinging between CS agents and Drivers and/or Passengers. I hope the above answers your question.

Thank you

What is changing in approach to MMM:

# Android vs iOS approach. (should take all the unnecessary uncertainty away and make models more sensitive)
# New approach to definition of period. Period will be defined not based on stabilised target variable, but as the smallest period with useful experiments and variablilty(increases/decreases). This also means that we are deciding on whether to trust/not trust a model based on how much variability it had.
# Potentially better approach to priors (will now not only be halfnormal, but TruncatedNormal to ensure bell-shaped results)
# Switch to more sensitive signup metric



What the models do not do:

* They’re not leading to new 'undiscovered' insights.

What they do:

* calibrate experiments results. They should align with them, but potentially they can even make them more accurate and prove that the impact of ads is more long-term than 2 weeks of experiment
* design a curve. We could make a curve ourselves based on the results of experiments. But since the model can sometimes see more variability, it can be more accurate than us. Overview:

[https://community.workday.com/node/1176833|https://community.workday.com/node/1176833]



1.

We now add a new Consolidated Invoice option on the Remittance Advice Type prompt on these tasks: 

* Create Customer Payment Application Rule
* Edit Customer Payment Application Rule

This enables you to create an advanced payment application rule to process customer payments referencing the consolidated invoice number entered in the Other Remittance Information section in the Remittance Advice grid.

This enhancement is available when you select these application types in the Application Rule Details section:

* On-Account Payment 
* Unapplied Payment

To process customer payments referencing a consolidated invoice instance in the Invoice column in the Remittance Advice grid, you must select the Limit to Referenced Invoices check box in the Application Rule Details section on these tasks.



2.

Workday now automatically applies customer payments to consolidated invoices referenced in the Invoice column and the Other Remittance Information section in the Remittance Advice grid using advanced customer payment application rules.

Workday processes customer payments for the consolidated invoice in this order:

* Credit adjustments.
* Negative invoices.
* Debit adjustments by the oldest invoice first: invoice date, then invoice ID.
* Regular invoices by oldest invoice first: invoice date, then invoice ID.

When there's a referenced consolidated invoice and an amount to pay specified on a remittance line, auto-apply processes the referenced consolidated invoice until the amount to pay is fully consumed.

We currently don't support this functionality for the:

* Cross-currency payments where the payment currency and invoice currency are different. 
* Multi-currency on-behalf-of payments with worktag balancing enabled.





3.



Workday now processes multiple consolidated invoices on a single remittance line referenced in the Invoice column in the grid when you run auto-apply with advanced payment application rules. Workday also processes multiple invoices based on 1 remittance advice line that references a purchase order number in the Other Remittance Information section on the remittance advice. 

Auto-apply will only process the first: 

* Consolidated invoice it encounters, when there's more than 1 consolidated invoice per remittance line in the Other Remittance Information section. 
* Purchase order number it encounters, when there's more than 1 purchase order number per remittance line in the Other Remittance Information section.



4.

We now update the Payment Applications grid on the View Customer Payment for Invoices report to populate:

* A Workday-delivered rule in the Customer Payment Application Rule field for payments applied with Workday-delivered rules. 
* The Consolidated Invoice field when you apply payments to consolidated invoices.

We add the enhancements on these tabs of the report:

* Payment Application 
* Application History

Overall, the logic from @romain.moisescot is correct.

The third option proposed by @sudipto.das would not work in my opinion. Why - because this would actually be covered not by the GDPR (this is common misconception), but by the [ePrivacy Directive|https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=CELEX%3A32002L0058] Art. 5(3).

The ePD will apply to any information, and not only personal data. So any act of accessing/obtaining data re/ the visitor`s usage of the website would require consent, unless it is needed for purposes: i) necessity to provide the website - like load balancing, etc. ii) necessary to provide the service - this, as I understand, could only be triggered where the user decides to register as the driver. 

There is also a third purpose where consents is not needed, that should not be applicable in this situation - to carry out the transmission of a communication over an electronic communications network.

Ss I see it, the lawful option to proceed would be the option 2 suggested by @alexander.fokau and confirmed by @romain.moisescot. I do not advise to change the approach.

Mainly related to data contracts, found some docs here: 

[https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/resource-configs/contract|https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/resource-configs/contract|smart-link] 

This is very relevant:

{quote}When the {{contract}} configuration is enforced, dbt will ensure that your model's returned dataset exactly matches the attributes you have defined in yaml:

* {{name}} and {{data_type}} for every column{quote}

As I understand it, dbt model will fail if SQL doesn’t correspond to data type defined in YML. So it doesn’t convert the data type, but it requires the script to return the correct data type. 

And from here: [https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/collaborate/govern/model-contracts|https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/collaborate/govern/model-contracts|smart-link] 

{quote}When building a model with a defined contract, dbt will do two things differently:

# dbt will run a "preflight" check to ensure that the model's query will return a set of columns with names and data types matching the ones you have defined. This check is agnostic to the order of columns specified in your model (SQL) or YAML spec.
# dbt will include the column names, data types, and constraints in the DDL statements it submits to the data platform, which will be enforced while building or updating the model's table.{quote}

Therefore, specifying column types in YML instead of letting dbt determine them automatically is out-of-the-box functionality 😉

What about Low and Moderate events? Can self-employed drivers be blocked/educated/warned?

The current guidelines are: 

* *Low and Moderate Events*: Drivers must not be contacted nor consequentially blocked for Low and Moderate Events. If the tool suggests a block, take a deviant action and select “Warning”. Communication (warnings) *must always go through to the Fleet Owners.* Do not send Educational messages. Rider blocks and communication can be handled as per SOPs.
Low, and Moderate risk events are automatically escalated to the _#es-safety-low-moderate-risk-blocking_ Slack channel for the local team’s visibility, once the tool is closed.

* *High and Significant Events*: +Fleet Drivers+ must not be contacted nor blocked for High and Significant Events. Communication *must always go through to the Fleet Owners.* Do not send Educational messages. +*Rider and Self-Employed Driver*+ blocks and communication can be handled as per SOPs. High and Significant risk events are automatically escalated to the _#es-rides-crisis-escalations_ Slack channel for the local team’s visibility, once the tool is submitted.

[~accountid:5caaf6edc39f203c28213595] for Treasury team it’s important to have the daily partner’s balances be available as soon as possible (it helps them with planning / predicting how much $$ we need to allocate to countries bank account → in short $$ savings in a long run right). 

If we would run our balance models daily (schedule = daily) this means the DAG triggers 00:00 UTC but we can’t be sure all the data is there at midnight UTC for all countries + we’ve got some countries like Paraguay, Mexico (soon Canada etc) whose local time is 18:00 PM when our daily DAG starts (at 00:00 UTC right) → the day is not finished for these partners yet. 

Hence we’ve got this [view|https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/blob/main/commerce_billing/models/debt/etl_billing_balance_timezones/etl_billing_balance_timezones.sql] which checks the city timezone (for us important is to build Americas balance later than Europe/Africa/Asia). So we pass a macro to the sql query e.g. for Providers like [this|https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/blob/main/commerce_billing/models/debt/etl_billing_balance_provider/etl_billing_balance_provider.sql]:

{noformat} and tz.world_timezone_bucket = {{ var("balance_timezone_bucket") }}{noformat}

If {{world_timezone_bucket}} = 1 then we know the timezone is Europe/Africa/Asia & the DAG will be triggered at 3am UTC (to give a few hours for ingestion from live) & if {{world_timezone_bucket}} = 2 then we know the timezone is for America & the DAG will be triggered at 9am UTC.

# the correctness of the convening of the shareholders' meeting - the lack of
# its capacity to adopt resolutions - none
# list the resolutions adopted - there is an indication of which resolutions were "adopted"
# the number of votes cast in favour of each resolution and the objections raised - none
# The minutes must be accompanied by an attendance list with the signatures of the participants of the shareholders' meeting and a list of shareholders voting by electronic means - none

In addition, pursuant to Article 231 § 1 of the Companies Act, the subject of the ordinary shareholders' meeting should be:

# examination and approval of the management report on the company's activities and the financial statements for the previous financial year - none (with regard to the management report on activities)
# adoption of a resolution on the distribution of profit or coverage of loss, if pursuant to Article 191 § 2 these matters are not excluded from the powers of the shareholders' meeting - there is an indication that such a resolution "was adopted"

*The Feature*

With Workday 2024R1, we add a Return Event Status As Created When Empty check box on the Edit Tenant Setup - Business Processes task that enables you to opt into displaying a Created status for business process events that have an empty status. When you select the check box, we display a Created status on:
• The Full Process Record.
• The View Event page.
• Custom reports. Some report fields might return a Created status when you use them in reports. Example: The Status report field.

When the Return Event Status As Created When Empty check box isn't enabled, you might notice unintentional behavior. Example: If you update information while completing the steps on the Change Job business process, we display the new value but don’t indicate what changed or display the previous value.

Workday recommends that you only enable the check box if business process events in your tenant currently returns a status of Created when the status is empty and you want to continue to view this status on events. By default, the check box isn't selected.

* In this form Bolt “declares, on honour, to perform the tender  in accordance with the content of the  specifications, in respect of which Bolt declares that it accepts, all its clauses without reservations”
* Making false declarations entails, as the case may be, the exclusion of the tender submitted and *constitutes a very serious administrative offence*, under the terms of article 456 of the Public Contracts Code, *which may result in the application of the ancillary sanction of deprivation of the right to participate,* as a candidate, as a competitor or as a member of a candidate or competitor group. member of a candidate or competitor group, *in any procedure adopted for the public procurement, without prejudice to reporting the offence to the competent authority for criminal prosecution.*
* Having read one page of the specifications I do not recommend submitting the form shared given the serious risks above. 
* In relation to the account of rentals, please note that rentals operates a localised business and no submission for Bolt Business in the name of the local entity is recommended in light of the potential tax implications.

For all tenders i suggest the following steps:

* that you read the documentation, particularly caderno de encargos
* should you be in doubt as to whether Bolt would be able to meet the commercial obligations, then see with the public entity whether there is still scope for Bolt to move on with a submission

Hi! Upon review of the [DPA|https://www.appsflyer.com/gatedpdfs/Data-Processing-Addendum-February2023-DPA.pdf] (should be the same as previously signed) - several regulatory points of concern were found + it does not fully align with our standards.

First, to highlight the most significant issues:

{color:#ff5630}*Major Risks (may cause regulatory problems/unlawful as per GDPR compliance):*{color}

1] *Link to the T&C broken:* [https://www.appsflyer.com/msa/|https://www.appsflyer.com/msa/] (Main Agreement) leads to 404 error - must be updated, otherwise we do not have the Main Agreement properly referenced.

*2] Data Deletion Post-Agreement Termination:* Rate limits for deletion requests are imposed, restricting Bolt's rights to data deletion unless additional fees are paid. This also applies when there is termination of the DPA. Arguably can be mitigated because the data can also be anonymised without restriction, but this should be an equal choice for Bolt.

*3] Data Breach Notification:* AppsFlyer does not commit to adhering to our mitigation instructions, and only promises to “consider” extra measures from Bolt's request. This should lead to the breach of the GDPR, as by law Applsflyer would have to 100% comply with our requests to implement additional safeguards.

They are also arguing that if they decide to implement those additional measures (at their own discretion), it will be at Bolt`s expense - which also raises concerns. I would change the wording to make sure this would only relate to unfounded and excessive requests.

In addition, there is no specified timeframe for notifying Bolt of a breach (referring to it as "without undue delay"), whereas our internal guidelines usually require a 24-hour notice period. 

4] *Audit Rights Limitation:* Bolt's right to request audits is restricted. AppsFlyer allows us terminating the agreement because it reserves the right avoid audits it deems “excessive” - which go beyond presenting Bolt with prior audit reports like SOC II or ISO27001.

Such audits are also limited to once annually unless prompted by a data breach or regulatory inquiry.

This is limiting our rights as the controller and would likely be unlawful.

5] *Being notified by Applsflyer in case they receive Bolt`s unlawful instruction*: “_Processor must inform the controller if, in its opinion, an instruction infringes the GDPR or other Union or Member State data protection provisions_” - *this requirement of the GDPR is not explicitly covered by the DPA.* 

This is basically a formal infringement of the GDPR Art. 28 - safeguard not ensured.

There is some wording to go around this obligation included in the DPA. Examples:

* _Customer specifically acknowledges and agrees that its use of the Services will not violate the rights of any Data Subject._
* _AppsFlyer shall not Process Customer Personal Data other than on the Customer’s documented reasonable and customary instructions_
* _Customer instructs AppsFlyer to Process Customer Personal Data in a manner consistent with the terms of the Agreement and this DPA._

But IMO, it will most likely be found non-compliant - as these do not safeguard us and Appslfyer if we accidentally give them an unlawful instruction. This is very unlikely to happen though, so its more of a formal risk.

{color:#0747a6}*More Minor Risks (associated with breaking our internal guidelines:*{color}

6] *Assistance with DPIAs and Supervisory Authorities:* Any assistance provided to Bolt in these matters will be at Bolt expense.

*7] Data Subject Request Notification:* No specific timeframe is provided, while we usually require notification within a maximum of 3 days.

*8] Liability:* The DPA does not specify liability arrangements, defaulting to the main agreement's terms - 350 K cap that were paid in the last 12 months - which is against our guidelines.

9] *International Data Transfers:* Compliance is generally met, except for updates related to Swiss SCCs, potentially leaving Swiss data subjects unprotected. This should be negligible as AFAIK we do not operate in Switzerland.

10] *Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) Governing Law and Forum:* The choice of Ireland is acceptable, though Estonia is preferred.

11] *General Authorisation of Sub-Processors:* the agreement allows for general authorisation with a 10-day objection period, contrary to our preference for specific authorisation and a maximum 20-day notice period.



*Mitigation if SCCs prevail*

Now, the majority of the above would be irrelevant if the agreement was between Bolt and Applsflyer in the USA.

Why - because then the EU SCCs would prevail, and in theory, many of the arrangements above would be substituted with the standard ones from the EU SCCs - including, inter alia, on audit, data breach, data deletion, etc.

Unfortunately, I see the Order Form is signed with the UK entity - which makes SCCs inapplicable.

*Summary - what we can do:*

1] Ideally, I would at least flag the “major problems” to Appsflyer so they could promptly provide some explanation and hopefully make changes.

2] We could also persuade them to sign the agreement with the USA entity instead. 

Finally, at our choice, we can disregard the risks and proceed “as is”, but IMO we do not want to do this.



I suggest let's try to flag the problems to them, and depending on their response and promptness, we could decide if we want to proceed before the deadline approaches.

+*Note to self*+

The ASA website provides guidance only as to the advertising rules. Generally, if there is a promotional advert then the rider would need to be aware of the terms surrounding the campaign (whether there is a requirement and steps to be taken etc).

The issue here is the marketing team have limited words that can be put on the Ad as Google Ads are not big enough to contain a lot of text and the marketing team want to know if it is sufficient to just contain a link to general terms. One way around this could be to draft special terms and conditions for this promotion and then provide a link to the special terms on the advert - this would be relatively low risk as long as the link is clearly visible and accessible to the user directing them to the special terms. 

+*Risk if you fall foul of the ASA*+ 

* the business may be notified and asked to remove the advert etc if it is misleading. 
* If the advert is not removed fines can be imposed. 
* The ASA can refer cases to Trading Standards.

+*Next steps*+

Hey [~accountid:60cdaa45a17463007061ed8e], thanks for raising this issue. 

We will draft a consent template for using photos. 

However, please note that consents to use photos taken from any online sources may turn out useless from legal aspect. Photos are protected by copyright and merchants can only give a consent to use photos for which they own copyright or for which they have a right to grant usage rights (e.g. based on agreements with authors/photographers). Experience shows that merchants often do not know or care about copyright. Therefore, we have a risk that if the consent proves wrong, our use of the photos will infringe the copyright of the actual rights holder. Meaning that we will be liable for the infringement and the actual copyright holder can request us to take down the photos and pay damages for unauthorised use. We cannot direct such claims to the merchants, but can only request compensation from the merchant later. If the merchant does not have money, we will not get any compensation.

Best,

Indrek

Thanks for looping me in [~accountid:712020:8c797c70-7a57-496e-aa3f-5d91df806eb2]! It’s especially valuable as I’m currently working on a comprehensive central legal assessment on the Ride Booker offering.

I wouldn’t take the route of argumentation you suggested for such cases. While due to the flow in the app etc the end users formally indeed remain the contracting parties to the service agreement then we consider Business customers to have basically equal rights to end users in that regard. _Our late amendments to the Delivery T&Cs we worked on together aim exactly to provide that transparency going forward and similar amendments will also be introduced to Rides T&Cs. So I wouldn’t deviate from this narrative to avoid confusing customers._

I’d rather rely on 6.4 (see also 2.3 and 3.2) of General T&Cs according to which the Customer is liable for all the activities of its representatives and Users (or see also c. 2.4. in special terms if applicable). And per 3.4 of General T&C all payments are non-refundable.

_Would we be discussing regular app rides here then we could argue that it’s a quite basic expectation that Users would ensure the rides are finished in their app (as far as we know Users could be cooperating with drivers on the fraud…) + ideally there’s language in the Rider T&C supporting this as well._ 

However with Ride Booker rides it’s trickier as Users don’t use the Rider app and have no obvious opportunity to check if the ride actually was finished. Nor do I believe it’s viable to argue that the Business customer admins (RB operators) would need to check that on ongoing basis. We should have better controls in place for RB to ensure drivers do not misuse the system (to detect if the time for the ride is too long). And should we really want to put more onus on the Business customer we should be more explicit about it in the T&Cs (which we currently are not).

All in all with regards to how to respond to the customer I’d consider making generic references to the above General T&C clauses (which principally are applicable also for RB) but agree on a reasonable refund as a gesture to clear this matter. E.g. the overcharged part of trips up to x months should we believe an average reasonable Business customer should have checked the reports and payment docs at least every couple of months or whatnot, and should have been able to detect the overcharge. Ofc subject to a business decision how large a reasonable refund should be to reduce both the risk of churn and demotivate the customer to pursue with the claim.

Cheers!

* Case 1: "My ride happened without me"
1. Full refund to the client and comment on driver’s profile
2. Comment on driver’s profile, full refund if needed
3. Comment on driver’s profile, full refund 

* Case 2: "I was charged more than expected". We receive requests when riders can be overcharged:
1. Investigating the reason of additional toll fee, compensating accordingly
2. Refunding extra amount to the customer, warning the driver (in 1st case)
3. Investigating the reason, acting accordingly to it

* Case 3: "My driver refused to pick me up"
1. Investigating, acting accordingly to the obtained information
2. Apologizing to the rider, no actions towards the driver, as there is a system block for such cases

Hey Hendrik!

I have reviewed both articles again and am having trouble understanding what the issue is.


The article you are referring to is[ 🚗 Rider did not get to the destination|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360013967819], which explains how much to compensate only for the situation when a rider did not get to the destination. And it says what to do depending on the distance of the final and requested destination. The same process regarding *how much to refund* is used for the UK.

As for the amount, if it falls under the “Final destination was *near* the requested destination” section, it should be equal to the smallest amount you can give in the UK market (as I understand, the option of giving promo codes in the UK exists, although it is not often used). This is explained within the article.

The article regarding the UK that is linked: [🚗 Refunding orders|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/9514453139858#refunding-orders-in-the-uk] explains *how* to refund orders within the UK.
The 3 examples noted there are only for “goodwill compensations”. So this is not connected to the [🚗 Rider did not get to the destination|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360013967819].

If there are any other situations that you need to compensate, it is required that you follow the proper procedure for it.
For instance, if the rider is complaining about the longer route, then you would need to follow the [🚗 Rider complains driver took a longer route|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360012505659] article.

If there is something still unclear, kindly provide more information and we will look into it.

h2. Update after meeting with Diana on 6/3

* Day of the workshop - 12/3 
* Main discussion topic: should CS agents assist the BA with the report of the problem or should they insist on the user who took the ride contacting us
* Objective of the workshop: deciding on the approach we want to take and which steps the process should contain
* Next steps:
** Diana to prepare a short overview of the problem, the pros and cons
** Possibly, Diana to prepare process maps for both versions of the process
** Diana to check if refunds are still done through Admin 

h2. Input we got from Quality & CS OPS 

{quote}*Input from Quality (they would like to keep the process as it is now):*
Important factor is efficiency → Saving time and enhancing process adherence.
Often, BAs have to spend considerable time reporting minor employee issues. In some markets, they even submit spreadsheets with 20–40 trips every week indicating ride issues, which BSSs can’t manage properly for time and experience reasons. By educating users on reporting through the Rider App, these tickets will be directed to the RH CS Backlog, which specializes in such matters, allowing our BSS to focus on business-related issues more efficiently.

*Input from CS OPS (they are open to changing the process):*
I believe that a better strategy is to avoid deflecting these contacts if possible and instead serve BAs when they arrive with these inquiries, unless we have some blockers. Here's my reasoning:

* Avoiding a deflection is a time save both for us and for admins and their employees - dealing with one incoming tickets instead of two or potentially more is an overall net gain for Bolt, and for admins it signals better convenience factor
* It results in better perception of our services - it shows us as more willing to support and resolve issues efficiently if we don't deflect, resulting in better customer satisfaction
* I also don't see any particular blockers to *not* deflect other than what [@ignacio.padillamelero|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U031WLHMFA6] stated. There is no privacy concern as far as I can see, and the data we would have access to would normally be sufficient to resolve most inquiries. There will be cases where it's more efficient to have the rider contact us (complex cases, cases where we lack information etc.) but in majority of the cases we can resolve these issues "just" from the admin contact and I don't see as much the need to deflect.

So I'm in favor of changing the process to avoid the deflection _unless_ any of the following is true:

* Inquiries about more than 3 orders at a time (it's an arbitrary number, but I think anything above 3 would become more burdensome for Business agents and would likely not be a big time gain over having B2C support handle these)
* Additional information is required from the rider - and here I don't mean just context of the issue, because I believe that we should trust and take the word of the BAs and we shouldn't require much more context than they have. But rather, hard info is missing that is entirely central to resolving a case, such as payment info, details of driver behavior etc. - basically, info that only the rider would know but that is 100% necessary to resolve the case).

Overall I think this change would have potential to improve our brand perception and user satisfaction with little to no downside, so it's a good opportunity to experiment with it.{quote}

I am definitely more in favor of us assisting the BA and not insisting that the user contacts us in all cases except for Safety.

Just a follow up. So far, we have not identified any legal blockers for processing payments made in one Territory by using the Processor located in the country where the card was issued. 

However, it looks like this is reduced to a contractual limitation. Every time we want to open a market and process payments with Adyen (for example), we sign affiliate agreements/addendums to include our subsidiaries to the main agreement every time we want to process payments in a new market (territory). 

These amendments are specific of the territory. For example, now for Canada. The affiliate agreement says "Merchant and Merchant Affiliate now wish Adyen to provide the Services as described in the Agreement to Merchant Affiliate for its business in the relevant region(s)."Meaning that our agreements are to process payments IN/WITHIN a territory, not payments FROM a Territory. So, based on this, I am not sure how we can (contractually speaking) process a card payment through that same country payment processor, despite of where it is used.

Then, there is another contractual issue from other perspective. Every time you use Bolt as a customer, you are obliged to the Terms and Conditions of that country where you are using the service.Our Terms and conditions are per country. The T&Cs says which Bolt entity (acting as agent of the Partner) will be charging the payment.So, if I go to lets say Azerbaijan, the payment should be in theory be charged by Bolt Services AZ LLC (as the agent of Drivers, correct? 

 So why then (if we make this optimisation change) I will be charged by another Bolt enity, whihc is not reflected in the T&Cs of that country where I took the ride?

After clearing/validating if this is legally possible from a global perspective, we need to make sure it is viable from a contractual perspective by reaching out to Adyen. And if so, then make the relevant changes in the T&Cs or include the provision in the new Payment terms.

Hey, all! 

I’ll outline the current workflow and the proposed workflow. Britta mentioned that the aim is *_not to breach_*, and the moderate events, that other teams are dealing with, can be picked up by case managers since the SLA is usually not 24 hours but 72.

This would affect notifications sent to *#cs-safety_rouk_notifications* channel.

Currently, we have three points on which the notification is created. Upon creation, we include a link to a pre-filled[https://www.cognitoforms.com/Taxify1/UKExternalReportingTemplate|https://www.cognitoforms.com/Taxify1/UKExternalReportingTemplate|smart-link]:
1.  All High/Significant events, upon creation of *Investigation*.
2. On the closure of Investigation, in some cases ({{Buckinghamshire}} Driver blocks, {{Driver Refuses Assistance Animal}} events, {{New Forest}} Driver HBs)
3. On the closure of the *Assessment*, 
- for specific events ({{Non-Accident Related Injury to Rider During Order, Driver Inappropriate Behaviour, Driver Fraudulently Asked More Money, Driver Contacted Rider After Journey, Driver Use of Hate Speech, Driver Discriminatory Acts Against Rider}})
- for combinations of events and licensing boroughs (for example, {{Driver Displays Road Rage}} for {{South Gloucestershire, Wirral, Southampton}})
- based on consequential (Only Low/Moderate events: {{Buckinghamshire}} Driver blocks, {{New Forest}} Driver HBs)

----

To notify the authorities quickly without the case managers' engagement within the first 24 hours, we would trigger a notification on the closure of the *Assessment tool*, based on the choice of {{Licensing City}} and {{Event Category}} ([here|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ffpp6qDNxNJbZEGh1K2I8_KCYkhvzw2R_BuAdVH6V8w/edit#gid=1445194297]).

Then, we’d put a link to a pre-filled [https://www.cognitoforms.com/Taxify1/RoUKAutomatedReporting|https://www.cognitoforms.com/Taxify1/RoUKAutomatedReporting|smart-link] form instead of a pre-filled External Reporting Template. A blank External Reporting Template link will be included, if a follow-up is needed. 

Why do we need a separate form,[https://www.cognitoforms.com/Taxify1/RoUKAutomatedReporting|https://www.cognitoforms.com/Taxify1/RoUKAutomatedReporting|smart-link] ?
- we need to gather additional details (_driver’s name, PHV, passenger’s details, copy-paste of a complaint_)
- to create a file, that will be later included in an e-mail to an authority

The notification looks like this and would be sent by a separate Bot, 
[+📩+|https://emojipedia.org/envelope-with-arrow] {{Automated Reporting to Council}}

!Screenshot 2024-03-06 at 16.49.59.png|width=100%!

After the form is complete and *“Finalise”* button is clicked, the e-mail with the file is automatically sent to a borough’s e-mail.

----

I believe we need to figure out how exactly the first and second parts are going to intersect, if so (_what do we do with consequential notifications, for example_).

*SQL query used*

{noformat}SELECT
    payment_method_type,
    gateway,
    scheme_id_exists,
    COUNT(*)
FROM
(
    SELECT
        p.gateway,
        p.payment_method_type,
        (
            CASE 
                WHEN (p.card_scheme_id IS NOT NULL) THEN 'yes'
                ELSE 'no'
            END
        ) AS scheme_id_exists
    FROM
        ng_public.payment_payment p
    WHERE
        p.created >= date '2024-02-28'
        AND p.state = 'captured'

Hi [~accountid:63f742f2e76fc61320f5dc0e] - thanks for reaching out on this. We understand the need to be competitive with pricing and therefore the legal team generally tries not to be ‘invasive / disruptive’ when it comes to how we set pricing etc., but there are a few principles worth setting out. 

+Background+

Bolt generally positions itself as ‘commercial agent’ for drivers and has the ability to set pricing for drivers in accordance with our knowledge of the market _(note: the UK is an exception - we provide the services and set the pricing for ourselves)_. However:

* all customers of the platform (and sometimes even drivers) are ‘consumers’ who should never be knowingly disadvantaged in any material / prejudicial way;
* we do not expressly reserve the right in our terms to vary prices on a experimental basis;
* it will be deeply annoying to drivers and customers to find out they have been subject to pricing variations (we do not want drivers to claim that we have cheated them out of fares);
* in some markets we are subject to restrictions on pricing and cannot deviate from published fares in accordance with transport regulatory requirements;
* we don’t want regulators taking an interest in this activity.

In summary, there’s some risk associated with it, which ought to be mitigated. 

+Mitigating Risk: principles+

The best way of mitigating this risk is the same for +*_all_*+ testing / experiments:

* we should only test when we commercially need to.
* the sum of the testing should not impact any person in any signifiant / material way.
* when we do test, ideally testing should be:
** restricted geographically (so not all persons are subject to tests);
** limited temporary (so it’s not constantly ongoing if this is not necessary); and
** otherwise limited to what is necessary to collect the data.

So the ask from the legal side is to please keep these principles in mind at all times. This will keep the activity as being what it is: an *_experiment_*. 

It’s accepted that it may not be possible to fully comply with all principles all of the time, but the main point is that we all look to mitigate risks where we can 💪 

+Proposal for Pricing (5% → 40%)+

Ultimately, your team will be best placed to know the value of ramping up the testing this much and it’s not for legal to say that this cannot be done. But it *_does_* seem quite an extreme jump: 40%, is this truly necessary? If we have lasted on 5% testing for this long, this would suggest otherwise.

My recommendation would be to first take into account the above principles, then incrementally increase the amount of testing by small amounts (for a geographically and temporarily limited period) to a point of diminishing returns, or to a point your team feels is ‘not excessive’ (considering the above principles), but then roll it back to a level where we are comfortable that the level of data is sufficient for our purposes. Also, care should be taken to ensure that the variances in the pricing are not large enough to be seen as significantly impacting anyone (for example, no double fares for the unlucky few). 

I hope that’s helpful enough for now - I will close the ticket but please keep me in the loop on any major developments and let me know if you’d like any further input.

# Are the road safety and ML training the only purposes for data processing?

Yes in a short term. In a long term we may use the information to detect and locate traffic signs and street names on buildings (potentially we could sell this information to the map makers). Ideally I’d include these options to avoid situation of reworking policies in the future.

# What set of features will be implemented for Oslo, Brussels and Nottingham respectively?

I wouldn’t split the features by cities. In general 

* we want to detect road surfaces (sidewalk detection) so we could apply certain restriction (lowering speed or forbidding the ride by completely stopping the scooter); 
* pedestrian nearby detection during the ride to lower the maximum allowed speed; 
* collect sidewalk riding and detected pedestrian cases for further reporting to cities (Oslo case) in anonymised way (just highlight areas where rides happen on sidewalks and rides with high density of pedestrians)
* parking quality check before ending the ride
* without the rider: parking check of scooters nearby (e.g., camera periodically is switched on to analyse the pakring quality of scooters nearby - highly unlikely that it will be implemented in some future)
* without the rider: location detection improvement (the scooter switches on the camera, sends a picture to the server so ops people could find the scooter for cases when GNSS either is not working or very imprecise)



# What service provider (Luna, Drover, or in-house solution) will be used for each market?

Drover for a while will be used in Oslo and in Nottingham for the whole period. And possibly in other cities where we go with OKAI fleet but commit to computer vision (Nottingham case) But the described above functionality is for in-house module.

Yes your statement is correct. You can link suppliers either via parent, or child. This means that your assumption is correct, that if you want to link child entities, then the parent supplier must be setup in the system. I’ll give the example of our Bolt entities, that could be in someone else’s system.

Let’s say that we have a customer who works with us, and they set some of our entities up as suppliers in their respective countries. We work with them in UK and Spain.

They have in our system two potential suppliers registered as: 

* Bolt Services UK Limited
* BOLTEST TXFY SL

But they won’t be able to link our entities, because our parent may be Bolt Technology OU. Therefore they would need to create that parent, and then link our children to it.

Same case applies for our suppliers with hierachies in Bolt, this will then allow you to clearly see spend across a whole group of entities, which is actually one global supplier. 🙂 

Happy to setup a call soon to discuss this potential process improvement, as supplier management improvements is a big area that we can make improvements on. * _(1) The Data Protection Inspectorate, the Financial Inspectorate, the Defense Police Agency, the Environmental Inspectorate, the Tax and Customs Board, and the Police and Border Guard Board may make a request to an electronic communications company about the data necessary to identify the end user related to the identification features used in the publicly available electronic communications network, with the exception of data related to the fact of message transmission._

Short answer is that there are two independent issues here that they have combined:

# The platform and technological solution is provided by separate entities and we cannot guarantee absolute update for the service - this can be affected from loss of data signal to web server outage. Bolt Drive service is dependant on the web platform and IoT and as long as it is not solved otherwise, there will be risk of random outage. Last I hear our uptime was somewhere 99,8%, but please don’t quote me on that. For example, service can be unavailable for the user if their profile is going through manual review or the app is outdated.
# Essentially the technical solution is dependent on 3 providers - IoT device, mobile coverage and Bolt Operations OÜ. Any interruption to any of these services will mean that the vehicle/service might not be accessible. In essence - SIA Bolt Services LV is providing the vehicles, but infrastructure for operating it is provided by other service providers.
# Essentially - the higher the service availability, the more expensive the service becomes. We cannot guarantee the service is always available and this is something that SIA Bolt Services LV cannot affect as this is set by the agreement concluded the rental service provider and platform provider.
# The consumer can present claims against Bolt as per 11.2 of the terms and conditions.

I have investigated this and this is the outcome:

The ultimate reason why the message ([SingleAttachmentMessageV2|https://github.com/bolteu/support-webview/blob/fd5753dbfe2c6232594273cf5c73df0ac733900a/src/views/SupportCase/components/Message/components/AttachmentsMessage/SingleAttachmentMessageV2.tsx]) gets re-rendered upon sending a new message is that the object reference to the [item|https://github.com/bolteu/support-webview/blob/fd5753dbfe2c6232594273cf5c73df0ac733900a/src/views/SupportCase/SupportCaseV2.tsx#L186] property passed to it is changing. It is because of the fact that messages are being [constructed based on events|https://github.com/bolteu/support-webview/blob/fd5753dbfe2c6232594273cf5c73df0ac733900a/src/views/SupportCase/SupportCaseV2.tsx#L113], and the [events list|https://github.com/bolteu/support-webview/blob/fd5753dbfe2c6232594273cf5c73df0ac733900a/src/views/SupportCase/SupportCaseV2.tsx#L37] changes every time there’s a new message - and that is because it’s [always replaced|https://github.com/bolteu/support-webview/blob/fd5753dbfe2c6232594273cf5c73df0ac733900a/src/slices/supportCaseSlice.ts#L37] with a new list from the API ([reducer|https://github.com/bolteu/support-webview/blob/fd5753dbfe2c6232594273cf5c73df0ac733900a/src/slices/supportCaseSlice.ts#L210]). That applies not only to the submitComment, but also other actions.

So in order to prevent the message from re-rendering, the reference should remain unchanged. This could be achieved in 2 ways:

1. Proper solution: Avoid all the messages being fetched from backend over and over again upon each and every new message event. Doing this (i.e. fetching only the new messages), based on the conversation with [~accountid:603cd5245290e700697a930b], would currently break the logic of e.g. interaction messages which may expire or change and are (as of now) expected to be re-rendered upon such event. So this is not an easy fix.

2. Client workaround: Updating the existing objects upon fetching all messages once again, in order to keep the reference. Unfortunately, the [messages returned from the API |https://github.com/bolteu/support-webview/blob/fd5753dbfe2c6232594273cf5c73df0ac733900a/src/api/types.ts#L118]are missing IDs, and it without those it wouldn’t be possible to match the messages in order to say which one’s which. Moreover, checking the server code, it seems that it’s not the middle-tier layer that is filtering out those IDs, but the [main service response|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/7b0e8c9f98a3d6a9381c5a61828ad14b73c7c964/gen/asyncApi/customer_support/CustomerSupportInternalAsyncApi.ts#L950] does not contain this ID either. So this is also not an easy fix.

With that, based on the discussion with [~accountid:639055925fce844d606d07b3], I’m dropping this ticket as there needs to be a major refactoring that should happen in order to accommodate that.

[+HERE+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/17sxnqyOazrLUsNAW_Zyzur1TFI_vN5LOBwj-8H36fbM/edit?usp=sharing] is the note from the call with Counsel on Platform Insurance on 5 March. KC to update his opinion. Appointed Representative request email sent to Allianz on 7 March:

Hi Cristina,

I apologise for the delayed response on this topic. However, I am now able to provide you with an update.

Our legal team has continued discussions regarding Bolt potentially falling under the FCA regulatory framework with our external counsel during my time in Berlin. As a result, the risks raised from the UK perspective, subject to formal advice Bolt is yet to receive, continue as two-fold:

# Bolt Estonia offering a financial promotion to passengers:

 

Bolt Estonia, as a party to the agreement, offering the UK passenger the opportunity by means of a promotion to enter into a regulated contract (contract of insurance) between Allianz and the passenger is deemed a regulated activity in the UK. Ordinarily, this alone could be solved by Bolt Estonia acquiring approval from a UK-authorised insurer - in this case, Allianz UK affiliate - for any insurance promotion put forward in the UK. Such approval by a UK-authorised insurer would fall outside the scope of the restrictions of financial promotions. Dependencies, why this solution alone most likely does not work relates to point 2 below.

# Bolt Estonia offering insurance coverage to UK passengers (arrangement of insurance):

 

Whilst this aspect is currently under further assessment, a continued risk has been raised for Bolt Estonia arranging insurance offerings in the UK for UK Passengers. It is likely that, while Bolt Estonia is the party to the insurance policy offering the insurance coverage from Estonia, an arrangement is made in the UK for the benefit of UK passengers. Such insurance offering (arrangement) is a regulated activity in the UK that falls under the supervision of FCA, requiring an appropriate FCA authorisation. For clarity, at this point, the regulated activity does extend to drivers, as the drivers in the scope for the insurance with Allianz have been pre-vetted by Bolt to operate as Private Hire Vehicles in the UK on Bolt’s platform.

Our UK regulatory external expert will conclude the risk of “arrangement of insurance” under point 2 to apply and Bolt Estonia is making arrangements for UK passengers, Bolt Estonia falls under a regulated activity in the UK. Subsequently, the solution under point 1 alone will not be sufficient. Therefore, the recommendation is that Bolt Estonia becomes an Appointed Representative (AR) of the Allianz UK affiliate. As a result of becoming an AR of Allianz UK affiliate, promotions under point 1 would also be subject to approvals by Allianz UK affiliate.

We are awaiting written confirmation of the advice and risks to us. However, it is crucial to understand whether Allianz will accommodate Bolt Estonia becoming an AR?



Please could you advise us of the steps to take for Bolt Estonia to become an AR of Allianz UK affiliate?

*23/02/2024* -  [Osborne Clarke’s email related to FCA risks|https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a34ul6IgEE7lP7LOVNkbSFMpVU-SdSQ2/view?usp=sharing] 

* The regulated activities associated with setting up and running the proposed pension  arrangements will, it appears, be conducted solely by Aviva Pensions and NOT Bolt. As such, *Bolt will not require authorisation or exemption to offer the proposed pension benefit to its drivers.*

To summarise:
The obligation to present allergens is derived from, inter alia, Articles 21 and 44 of Regulation No. 1169/2011 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 October 2011 on the provision of food information to consumers.
In polish law the issue of how the information above should be provided was clarified by the Regulation of the Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development of 23 December 2014 on the labelling of particular types of foodstuffs (Journal of Laws of 2015, item 29). In particular according to § 19 point 2 of the Regulation: “*The information referred to in point 1* [which is inter alia article 21 of the Regulation No. 1169/2011 of the European Parliament] *shall be given at the point of sale on a display relating to the food or otherwise in a place directly accessible to the final consumer."*
*Polish sanitary-epidemiological authorities expressly stated that such information CAN NOT be provided only orally on a client’s request.*
Given the above, your way of informing users about allergens contained in the menu (direct telephone contact with the provider) *is indeed not compliant with the polish law.* The information should be *provided in an easily accessible written form*, which in our situation can be link or a document.

Hi [~accountid:610a3ee66051c5006aeeeea1] and [~accountid:712020:0641ea87-e832-482b-8673-ab85e9ad6441] 

As agreed, I just finished reviewing the analysis made by DLA when Bolt first started onboarding Taxis on the platform. 

Firstly, there is one main conclusion of the analysis that is not applicable now, given the alterations to the Taxi Law, being that the Law now provides guidance on the availability of Taxi services on electronic platforms, which did not happen before. 

In order to fully access what has changed and what are the implications now, I believe we have to make further analysis of the differences between the old and new Taxi regime. Let me know if you want me to start doing that. 

Regarding the “Documento de Cálculo do Preço”: 

# Usually, Taxi services prices are determined by law (fixed fees). 
# Both the old and the new law do allow for a special pricing regime called “price by contract”, which allows the price to depart from the regulated rates. The agreement must be made in writing, and for a period of not less than 30 days. This solution provides the customer with a specific price before the ride, instead of an estimate which would be based on the regulated tariffs. The taxi driver operating under this option does not use the taximeter to determine the price of the ride.
# This “by contract” pricing system has been the one used by Bolt since the Taxi onboarding, hence why there is this document with prices being shared with the drivers. 
# Contrarily to what I was thinking before, these fees are not public information, in the sense that they are determined by law, but they can be considered business secrets. 
# Therefore, as this document constitutes a pricing contract, it has to be agreed by both parties. 
# That being, it should be clearly declared as accepted by the drivers onboarding the platform.

*Date:* 02.11.24 

*Start time:* 11:00am

*End time:* 11:38

*Present:* Aisling Dunne, Anusha Balachandre

*Background information*

* E-scooters have been illegal and in June primary legislation passed all stages date and it was signed into law at the end of June.
* A week later the draft regulations were published in early July and the Irish government sent them to the European Commission under the Tris procedure, this procedure is where you are setting vehicle standards.
* All European member states have to publish their standards, no other EU member state have served their procedure, EU member states had 90 days to apply, closing date was 6 October, provided there is no concerns raised, the department have raised that the regulations will come out in November.

* In the primary legislation, the max weight, power and speed was flagged with the department that most scooters operate above that. Aisling has said that the Minister can only adapt down not adapt up with the legislation. However the minister is saying he cannot adapt up to 25kg.

Hi [~accountid:712020:5c3f18cd-53ab-40ca-9fae-fb38035ab6d8], 

Thanks for clarifying the request. In Norway, when a person or a company declares bankruptcy, their assets are typically transferred to a bankruptcy estate. The bankruptcy estate is managed by a trustee appointed by the court. The primary purpose of the bankruptcy estate is to liquidate the assets of the bankrupt entity and distribute the proceeds to creditors according to the established priority of claims.

The estate has certain rights against creditors that the creditors are obliged to respect. The purpose of the bankruptcy estate is that the estate shall “steps into the shoes” of the bankruptcy debtor and seize all the debtor’s assets and claims. This gives the estate, among others, the following rights: 

* The estate may collect the debtor’s bank deposits, the debtor’s receivables and other claims held by the debtor.
* The trustee of the bankruptcy estate has the authority to investigate transactions made by the bankrupt entity prior to the bankruptcy filing, especially those that may be considered preferential or fraudulent. 

Based on the above, my assessment would be that the request falls within the authority of the estate and that no further clarifications are required.

Michelle

Aisling asked the legal team on which entity would go for tendering when e-Scooters are legalised in Ireland. AB provided Aisling with the following information: 

Rentals business operates three different business models:

* cross border (where Bolt Ops OU owns the fleet and offers the rental services)
* semi-localised (where the local entity owns the fleet and offers the rental services, Bolt Ops offers the App and collects payments)
* fully-localised (the local entity owns the fleet, offers the rental services, is contractually responsible for offering the Bolt App and collects it's own payments)

Ireland is currently operating an e-bike fleet. So whichever business model is operating the e-bike business, it would follow the same for scooters

If Ireland is semi-localised and the local entity is the consumer facing "rental services provider" (also reflected in T&Cs) then it is the local entity that should apply for a tender and/or contract with local municipalities.

+*UPDATE ON THE CURRENT STATUS OF E-SCOOTERS BECOMING LEGALISED IN IRELAND*+

*Date:* 23 January 2024

*Time:* 11am - 11.45am

*Present:* [~accountid:610279859798100070592384] and [~accountid:63fe21787c30bbd6b33e09d3]

*Discussion:* Launch of e-Scooters in Ireland update

There is currently a hold, and this is due to the legislation requirements being approved by the minister. AD said that it is her understanding that the regulations covers e-Bikes, and addresses e-Bikes with a throttle (and this is where the current hold up is, the hold up is not to do with e-Scooters). Bolt does not have any throttle bikes in Ireland therefore this does not have any consequences for Bolt.

+*Legislation outlines the following requirements for e-Scooters in Ireland*+

*Max weight - 25kg*

*Max speed - 20km*

*Max unrated power of - 500 watt*

The e-Scooter that will be launched is the Bolt 4 (The Cobra) this is the only scooter that meets the specifications outlined in the legislation and it is reliable. The downfall is that newer models have been released that have features such as indicators and suspension and the Bolt 4 does not have this.

Bolts sensors are on the 4, 5, 6 and a lot of the software updates apply to all scooters, this is because lots of the features are software as opposed to hardware.

The Bolt 4 was made by Bolt to order.

They are considering renaming the Bolt 4 for Ireland, not confirmed yet.

+*Background information on e-Scooters*+

*Bolt 4 (the cobra)*- [See here|https://bolt.eu/en/blog/bolt-launches-new-fourth-generation-scooter-model/]

*Bolt 5 (the Okai)* - [See here|https://bolt.eu/en/scooters/], this was made by a company Okai (this company manufacturers scooters for all competitor companies), loads of companies have the same scooter, Bolt has less control on modifying these, there has been a few difficulties with the Bolt 5.

*Bolt 6 (the Cobra)* - [See here|https://bolt.eu/en/blog/introducing-bolt-6-scooter/], the 6 is cheaper than buying an Okai from another company, and the reason is because Bolt is making these, these scooters are being made in China and being assembled in Tallinn

It would be preferred by the team in Ireland that Bolt would be launching the Bolt 6, as there is more safety features and it is the newest scooter, unfortunately due to the regulations in Ireland, Ireland can only launch the 4. Separately to that, there is a supply chain issue, and due to Bolt winning a lot of tenders (Milan, Brussels, and Oslo) in priority 1 cities there is an issue on supply.

FYI - A priority 1 city is a city that is big in size, has lots of potential revenue.

+*What are the competitors doing*+

Tier lightest scooter is 27kg, they are exploring changing the battery to get the scooters in the 25kg mark.

Super predestrian - they are gone.

Dot - do not have an option of a lighter scooter.

Voi - do have an option of a lighter scooter.

Due to the regulations only 3/4 out of the 7 competitors can launch in Ireland with scooters that meet the regulations specifications.

+*Background timeline of why there has been delays*+

Primary legislation signed in June 2023 - this then went to the European Commission for the tris procedure (which is when this is sent to all member states for 90 days for them to flag if there are any concerns) - The tris procedure ran from June 2023 - October 2023 the 90 days were up - European Commission come back to Ireland said they are good to go with those regulations. Then Ireland expected it to be signed as it has gone on for 4 years. Week before Christmas, [~accountid:610279859798100070592384] spoke to the person project managing it, the issue is with the throttle and the e-Bike, they are trying to get everyone onboard. Ireland thought it would be Nov/Dec, however regulations have not been signed yet.

+*Council Bi-Laws*+

On the same day the minister signs the regulations, it is expected that the minister will bring in council guidelines at same time he signs the regulations. The guidelines purpose is to include bi-laws in an effort for all citifies to be the same page.

Ireland team have not seen the guidelines yet, [~accountid:610279859798100070592384] is hoping that Bolt would have had a positive influence on the guidelines and [~accountid:610279859798100070592384] has been having discussions regarding these.

*Expected timeframe:* February 2024

+*Which cities will Ireland team be launching*+

Sligo has agreed in draft that Bolt can launch there

Carlow has signed and agreed that Bolt can launch there

Bray - They have said they are interested once scooters are legal in Ireland

Sligo template once it is finalised will be applicable for other markets, Bolt has won Port Leashe
