Hi [~accountid:6257f823ed2b3e0074fd8114] 

After analysing this issue we have concluded the following: 

* Taxi services are regulated by a Law that was amended last October. The new Law has specific provisions that regard the provision of these services through electronic platforms. We are going to further analyse the impact of the legislative changes on our activity.  
* Both the old and the new law do allow for a special pricing regime called “price by contract”, which allows the price to depart from the regulated rates. The agreement must be made in writing, and for a period of not less than 30 days. This solution provides the customer with a specific price before the ride, instead of an estimate which would be based on the regulated tariffs. The taxi driver operating under this option does not use the taximeter to determine the price of the ride.
* This “by contract” pricing system has been the one used by Bolt since the Taxi onboarding, hence why there is this document with prices being shared with the drivers. Therefore, the pricing document could be considered a contract between Bolt and the drivers, meaning it could be considered sensitive business information. 
* Therefore, although there is no legal prohibition to join this document to the T&Cs, you need to decide whether it is ok to publicly reveal this information. 
* If you consider it is ok to share the information together with the T&Cs, then you don’t need to send the document to each driver individually, but rather make it available as the drivers are signing in to the platform and accepting the T&Cs. 
* If you consider it is not ok to share the information, because you don’t want to make it publicly available, it is also ok to share it through Life Cycle Comms, considering that, as this document constitutes a contract, it needs to be explicitly accepted by the driver. 



In sum, the answer to your questions are:

# *_Would it be possible to include the "Documento de Cálculo de Preço de Viagem" as an Attachment to the Taxi Operators T&Cs_**?* Yes, there is no legal provision prohibiting that but you have to access whether you want to make this pricing document public, as T&Cs are public documents.  
# *I**_f we include this document either in the T&C's or the Life Cycle Comms after a fleet is signed up, could we consider that this document is delivered with this method?_* Yes, if the Document is next to the T&Cs, when the user accepts the T&Cs they are automatically accepting the Annex. If not, the document can be sent through Life Cycle Comms given that the driver has the opportunity to accept the fees.

Please let me know if you have any doubts.

*What personal data do we process?*

When you use our Bolt rental electric scooters, we process your personal data collected via the sensors of the scooter to ensure you are using our services in a safe manner. The type of data we process from scooters includes geolocation data, vehicle speed, motor power (including voltage and throttle level) and driving style information (including sudden braking or skidding). This data is used to identify reckless driving events, i.e. skidding, abrupt braking, tandem riding, bad parking and collisions.

*How do we process your personal data?*

Our internal monitoring system tracks each event that occurs whilst a user is using the scooter, assigns it a certain weight, then calculates an overall score for reckless driving and issues a warning once the user reaches a certain score threshold. The total score of the user is the sum of the reckless events over the last five rides.

If we detect any potentially dangerous behaviour then we will issue the user with a warning in the app to encourage them to refrain from using the scooter in a certain way. There are three levels of warnings:

#  *first warning* - informs the user about the risks of misbehaviour;
#  *second warning* - limits the speed of the scooter until the overall user score improves; and
#  *third warning* - temporarily suspends the user from the service. The user is able to contest the suspension by contacting our Customer Support Team for further information as to why their account was suspended.

Pros and cons.

+*NEW STATUS*+

*Pros*

* Existing tooling (admin filter, db index, data replication, lifecycle events etc.) -> faster development
* Usage of statuses is well known and natural for ops -> easier adoption

*Cons*

* to restore previous status we need to save it somewhere (it could be IN_PROGRESS or RESUBMISSION_NEEDED), or introduce 2 new statuses: non_responsive_in_progress and non_responsive_document_resubmission_needed
* New status requires update of all places where we check for status



+*STORED PROPERTY*+

*Pros*

* Will not affect any existing logic -> less risk of bugs

*Cons*

* Need to create all the tooling  (admin filter, db index, data replication, lifecycle events etc.) 
* New DB column will either make queries slower or require adding several new indexes and increase table weight
* Harder to explain to ops, because they are used to “status” concept, they see own workflow in statuses



+*VIRTUAL PROPERTY*+ *(BASED ON LAST_UPDATE)*

*Pros*

* We do not need to create column in DB
* We do not need to setup any background job to set property, also we do not need logic that will unset it after changes
* Will not affect any existing logic -> less risk of bugs

*Cons*

* We have less control over the logic of setting and unsetting
* Need to create all the tooling  (admin filter, db index, data replication, lifecycle events etc.) 
* New SQL condition will either make queries slower or require adding several new indexes and increase table weight
* Harder to explain to ops, because they are used to “status” concept, they see own workflow in statuses

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

channel_platform_combinations = pd.unique(df[['channel', 'platform']].agg('-'.join, axis=1))
colors = plt.cm.tab10(np.linspace(0, 1, len(channel_platform_combinations)))

# Creating a dictionary to map each channel+platform combination to a color
color_map = {combination: colors[i] for i, combination in enumerate(channel_platform_combinations)}

def calculate_ftrs(vmax, x_values):
    return vmax * x_values / (vmax + x_values)

x_values = np.linspace(0, 700, 100)

# Recreate the plots for each city
cities = df['city'].unique()
plots = {city: df[df['city'] == city] for city in cities}

# Generating the plots with consistent colors for each channel+platform combination
for city, city_data in plots.items():
    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
    
    for i, row in city_data.iterrows():
        label = f"{row['channel']} {row['platform']}"
        combination = f"{row['channel']}-{row['platform']}"
        # Ensure the color is consistent with previously defined combinations
        if combination in color_map:
            color = color_map[combination]
        else:
            # This is a new combination, assign a new color
            new_idx = len(color_map)
            color_map[combination] = colors(new_idx)
            color = color_map[combination]
        
        # Plot the main curve
        plt.plot(x_values, calculate_ftrs(row['vmax_mean'], x_values), label=label, color=color)
        
        # Plot credible intervals as filled areas
        plt.fill_between(x_values, 
                         calculate_ftrs(row['vmax_lower'], x_values), 
                         calculate_ftrs(row['vmax_higher'], x_values), alpha=0.2, color=color)
    
    plt.title(f"Cost Efficiency Curve for {city}")
    plt.xlabel("Cost")
    plt.ylabel("FTRs")
    plt.legend()
    plt.xlim(0, 700)
    plt.grid(True)
    plt.show(){noformat}

Hello, Victoria!

Thank you for these great questions.

The Standard Operating Procedures for Product Safety which are outlined in Confluence/Knowledge Base apply to safety incidents which have taken place on our platform, meaning during an active order. 

The only exception is the event Non-Platform Safeguarding, which by definition is a safety incident we would want to note and take protective measures against, but which takes place outside of our platform (i.e not during an active delivery order) and involves a Bolt user.

# These would fall under Non-Platform Safeguarding if they did not take place during the order, but unfortunately we can’t do much if we can not identify the courier. If we’d be able to identify the courier in both cases, we could also try to find out if these events took place during an active order or not. If they’d have taken place during an order, only then we’d be able to log Courier Use of Hate Speech or the Vehicle Accident. 
# I doubt oil leaking from their vehicle is malicious behaviour. Please note that the event Courier Maliciously Damaged Property should only be used if there’s actual intention by the courier to damage eater/provider’s property, e.g. hitting the fence with their foot and breaking the fence. 
# Possibly this can be logged under Non-Platform Safeguarding, but it’s difficult to say without viewing the actual case. 
# You are correct saying there is a thin line, but if the courier did not feel threatened and the order was eventually paid, I’d suggest to consider this non-safety. If the eater doesn’t want to pay for their order, these guidelines can be followed under the non-safety section: [Eater did not pay or paid less|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360015355199].

Michelle kindly provided me with some background on these type of requests in another ticket.

For a bit of background on bankruptcy estate requests from Norway when a person in Norway or a company declares bankruptcy, their assets are typically transferred to a bankruptcy estate. The bankruptcy estate is managed by a trustee appointed by the court. The primary purpose of the bankruptcy estate is to liquidate the assets of the bankrupt entity and distribute the proceeds to creditors according to the established priority of claims.

The estate has certain rights against creditors that the creditors are obliged to respect. The purpose of the bankruptcy estate is that the estate shall “steps into the shoes” of the bankruptcy debtor and seize all the debtor’s assets and claims. This gives the estate, among others, the following rights:

* The estate may collect the debtor’s bank deposits, the debtor’s receivables and other claims held by the debtor.
* The trustee of the bankruptcy estate has the authority to investigate transactions made by the bankrupt entity prior to the bankruptcy filing, especially those that may be considered preferential or fraudulent.

+*International transfers*+ 

In circumstances where an adequacy decision adopted by the European Commission does not apply, the legal basis that we rely on for the transfers of personal data to the recipients that are located outside of the EU/EEA is the Standard Contractual Clauses adopted by the EU Commission (on June 4, 2021). 

+*Retention*+

Bolt retains your data for only as long as necessary for the purposes described above. This means that we retain different categories of data for different periods of time depending on the type of data, the transportation service it relates to, and the purposes for which we collected the data.

* Your personal data will be stored as long as you have an active account. If your account is closed, personal data will be deleted (according to our retention schedule and rules), unless such data is still required to meet any legal obligation, or for accounting, dispute resolution or fraud prevention purposes.
* Financial data regarding transportation services provided to passengers will be stored for three years after the last journey. Data required for other accounting purposes will be stored for seven years after the last journey.
* In the event of a suspected criminal offence, fraudulent activity or false information having been provided, the data will be stored for up to 10 years.
* In case of payment disputes, data will be retained until the claim is satisfied or the expiry date of such claims.
* Journey history data and the data about usage of transportation services will be stored for three years, after which the data will be anonymised.
* Data on sensors for rental vehicles is stored for 6 months.

Please note that the deinstallation of Bolt app in your device does not cause the deletion of your personal data. If the Bolt app has not been used for three years, we’ll get in touch and ask you to confirm whether you wish to keep your account active for future use. If no reply is received in a reasonable time, the account will be closed and personal data will be deleted unless such data is required for any purpose mentioned earlier in this privacy notice.

 

+*Source of Personal Data*+

Your personal data originates from either your direct provision to Bolt or its collection through the Bolt platform.

*_Personal Data we collect about you from other sources_*

*User Rating*
We collect personal data about you, including feedback and ratings from the Drivers, after each trip. The ratings are displayed as an average and are anonymous. You will not see individual ratings linked to a specific trip or person.

 

+*Automated decision-making if you are a user of the rental services*+

*What personal data do we process?*

When you use our Bolt rental electric scooters, we process your personal data collected via the sensors of the scooter to ensure you are using our services in a safe manner. The type of data we process from scooters includes geolocation data, vehicle speed, motor power (including voltage and throttle level) and driving style information (including sudden braking or skidding). This data is used to identify reckless driving events, i.e. skidding, abrupt braking, tandem riding, bad parking and collisions.

*How do we process your personal data?*

Our internal monitoring system tracks each event that occurs whilst a user is using the scooter, assigns it a certain weight, then calculates an overall score for reckless driving and issues a warning once the user reaches a certain score threshold. The total score of the user is the sum of the reckless events over the last five rides.

If we detect any potentially dangerous behaviour then we will issue the user with a warning in the app to encourage them to refrain from using the scooter in a certain way. There are three levels of warnings:

#  *first warning* - informs the user about the risks of misbehaviour;
#  *second warning* - limits the speed of the scooter until the overall user score improves; and
#  *third warning* - temporarily suspends the user from the service. The user is able to contest the suspension by contacting our Customer Support Team for further information as to why their account was suspended.

For safety considerations, we cannot disclose the exact thresholds that trigger our warnings to prevent users from abusing the system.

We may also use automated decision-making in order to undertake fraud checks which are necessary for us to perform our services, ensure that the services are paid for and ensure the protection of riders from fraudulent transactions on their payment cards.

We may use automated decision-making in order to verify you which is necessary to ensure the safety of our platform and the enforcement of our terms and conditions.

We may also use automated decision-making for complaint resolution purposes. We may use the complaints information you provide to our customer support team via our chat function. The information relating to your complaints may be used to generate an automated response which will then be evaluated by a human agent to make the final decision.

In cases where we use automated processing or profiling that has a significant effect on your rights, you may have the right for human intervention and the right on grounds relating to your particular situation to object to the processing of personal data concerning you based on automated decisions/profiling as set out in section “Your rights and controls”, and to express your point of view and contest the outcome of the decision by contacting our customer support in our app.You may also be entitled to an explanation regarding the logic of making an automated decision.

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [Privātums|https://bolt.eu/lv-lv/privacy/]  .

*Your rights*

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws.

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

Hi @johannes.varkki, chiming in to try and help here as I'm a bit closer to South Africa's data protection law and legal systems.

Section 205 Subpoena

The Investigating Officer in this ticket is proposing to subpoena (force) a Bolt representative to appear before a Magistrate to provide the information — they have the power to do this under South Africa's Criminal Procedure Act (s 205). We should avoid going through this process as it is time consuming and requires in-person legal support (cc @georgia.barnard).  

POPIA s6 Exclusions

I want to highlight that South Africa's data protection law does not apply to Public Bodies (like the South African Police Services) where:

the purpose of which is the prevention, detection, including assistance in the identification of the proceeds of unlawful activities and the combating of money laundering activities, investigation or proof of offences, the prosecution of offenders or the execution of sentences or security measures, to the extent that adequate safeguards have been established in legislation for the protection of such personal information (s3 POPIA).

This exclusion applies provided that the SAPS implements safeguards to protect the data — something that we can't assess for them, however, it is important to note that SAPS were recently investigated by the South African Data Protection Regulator and it was found that they do not have appropriate safeguards in place to protect data they receive.

General thoughts

There is no explicit right to access/receive information that SAPS can refer to in the requested letter, but they are exempted from data protection law provisions under certain circumstances. 

I am comfortable that we can provide the requested information to the Investigating Officer.

Hey [~accountid:60c88e6e8f2cc1006909fcf6] ! 

A while ago, I discussed a similar question with Lukas concerning the Benme company, which is also an employee benefit platform. The concern is that if they start offering our coupons, we may lose potential clients who might think that since Bolt is available in Benme, they do not need to continue using Bolt Business.

* The current T&C do not protect us from such cases. Additionally, clause 2.5 does not state that the reselling of our services is unlawful. Thus, I would not rely on this clause.
* The proposed solution is to add necessary protective clauses to the Special Terms if we decide to cooperate with such platforms. Several scenarios are offered below:
*# Prohibition of selling coupons to Business clients' customers in general. If they start reselling our coupons to their clients, it will constitute a material breach of the agreement, allowing Bolt to exit immediately, along with a penalty clause. This clause would ensure limited use of our coupons, allowing the platform to use them only for its own purposes, its employees, and service providers, not customers.
*# Another solution is to allow the use of coupons for Bolt business clients' customers only if explicitly allowed by Bolt. In this case, a platform needs to reach out to us if any of their clients want to use Bolt coupons. We then check internally if this company is already our client. If yes, permission is not granted, and the platform shall refuse to offer our coupons to a specific company. If a company is not our client, we give permission.
*# Per their suggestion, we can also create a list of companies they can work with (although I am not sure if we can come up with such a list, therefore approving companies one by one per option “b“ seems better to me). If we discover that they work with companies they are not allowed to, it will constitute a material breach of the agreement, allowing Bolt to exit immediately. We can also introduce a penalty clause if they are in breach.

BUT there is a possibility that we will not discover the breach. Also, every company we allow them to offer our coupons to means that we are potentially losing this company as our future direct client. Thus, the general question to the business is: should we allow such platforms to resell our services in general, or do we allow the use of our services for clients' employees only (option “a“)?

Let me know if you have any thoughts/questions!

Hi [~accountid:61124fbaec92ab0070270a0b] I will close this ticket but will summarise here the regulatory matters discussed at the time this ticket was opened. I will also update the Portugal Legal knowledge page in confluence for future memory:

* article 8(3) Law n.o 45/2018 determines that “_Pet animals may not be refused transport, provided they are properly accompanied and_ +_secured_+_, unless there is a reasonable reason, such as danger, state of health or hygiene._” 
* Additionally, the same law determines in article 6(5) that “_it is compulsory to carry guide dogs for blind passengers._” [DL 74/2007|https://diariodarepublica.pt/dr/detalhe/decreto-lei/74-2007-520261] defines guide dog as “_a dog that has been trained or is being trained to help visually impaired people_” and explains that these dogs are not required to wear a functional muzzle. 
* article 14(2) establishes “the operator of the electronic platform must block access to the services provided by the platform by … drivers … that fail to comply with any of the requirements referred to in this law”. Therefore it would appear that Bolt would have the right to block drivers that fail to comply with the TVDE law, including the obligations regarding the transportation of pets and guide-dogs.
* Accordingly, our TVDE operator terms and conditions clarifies that we may suspend any access to a driver account, without any prior notice, in the event of a material or repeated breach by the TVDE Operator of any of its obligations under the Agreement and/or of any applicable laws or regulations. 

Therefore, the refusal of drivers to take people with pets (under the right circumstances) and assistance animals gives Bolt the right to block them. However, like other compliance related blockings I would implement a reasonable approach and provide the opportunity to drivers to ensure compliance in the future.

*SQL query used*

{noformat}SELECT
    gateway,
    payment_method_type,
    is_eea_country,
    country,
    scheme_id_exists,
    COUNT(*)
FROM
    (
    SELECT
        p.payment_method_type,
        p.gateway,
        sc.country_code AS country,
        (
            CASE 
                WHEN (p.card_scheme_id IS NOT NULL) THEN 'yes'
                ELSE 'no'
            END
        ) AS scheme_id_exists,
        (
            CASE 
                WHEN (sc.country_code IN (
                    'at', 'be', 'bg', 'hr', 'cy', 'cz', 'dk', 'ee', 'fi', 'fr', 'de', 'gr', 'hu', 'ie', 'it', 'lv', 'lt', 'lu', 'mt', 'nl', 'pl', 'pt', 'ro', 'sk', 'si', 'es', 'se', 'gb', 'gf', 'gp', 'mq', 'me', 'yt', 're', 'mf', 'gi', 'ax', 'pm', 'gl', 'bl', 'sx', 'aw', 'cw', 'wf', 'pf', 'nc', 'tf', 'ai', 'bm', 'io', 'vg', 'ky', 'fk', 'ms', 'pn', 'sh', 'gs', 'tc', 'ad', 'li', 'mc', 'sm', 'va', 'je', 'gg', 'gi'
                )) THEN 'yes'
                ELSE 'no'
            END
        ) AS is_eea_country
    FROM
        ng_public.payment_payment p
    JOIN ng_public.payment_payment_order po
        ON
        p.payment_order_id = po.id
    JOIN ng_public.admin_system_city sc
        ON po.city_id = sc.id
    WHERE
        p.created >= date '2024-02-28'
        AND p.state = 'captured'
        AND p.payment_method_type IN (
            'applepay',
            'googlepay',
            'processout'
        )
)
WHERE 
    scheme_id_exists = 'no'
GROUP BY
    gateway,
    payment_method_type,
    is_eea_country,
    country,
    scheme_id_exists
ORDER BY
    gateway,
    payment_method_type,
    is_eea_country,
    country,
    scheme_id_exists
LIMIT 100
;
{noformat}
